title_jp: {食料品|しょくりょうひん}の{消費税|しょうひぜい}が1%に？
context: Thursday evening: アルちゃん is back from {鷹見岳|たかみだけ} before dark, and over dinner {恵子|けいこ}さん shows him a simplified news article. On 6 November 2026 the lower house passed a bill cutting the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% for two years from April 2027; the upper house began debating it on 11 November, where the ruling parties lack a majority. Source: Jiji Press (Nippon.com), Yomiuri Shimbun.
scene: Back from your hike, {恵子|けいこ}さん shows you the news: the tax on food may drop to 1%. But why 1%, not zero?

phrases.jp: {温かい|あたたかい}うちに{食べて|たべて}ね。{山|やま}、{疲れた|つかれた}でしょう？
phrases.en: Eat it while it's warm. The mountain must have tired you out, right?
phrases.note: {温|あたた}かいうちに{食|た}べて is what every Japanese mum says at the table.

phrases.jp: {安い|やすい}うちに、お{米|こめ}を{買って|かって}おこうかな。
phrases.en: Maybe I'll buy rice while it's cheap.
phrases.note: 〜ておこうかな = 'maybe I'll do it now, to be ready'. Half talking to yourself.

phrases.jp: どうして0%じゃなくて1%なんですか？
phrases.note: 〜んですか asks for the reason or story behind something. Without ん it sounds flatter.

phrases.jp: {最近|さいきん}{何|なん}でも{高い|たかい}から、{助かる|たすかる|to be a help, a relief|4}わ。
phrases.en: Everything's expensive lately, so it'll be a real help.
phrases.note: わ at the end is soft and a bit old-fashioned feminine: you'll hear it from women {恵子|けいこ}さん's age.

phrases.jp: {安く|やすく}なるのはいいけど、お{金|かね}はどこから{出す|だす}{ずら||(Nagano dialect) = だろう, I wonder|1}。
phrases.en: It's nice that things get cheaper, but where's the money going to come from, I wonder.
phrases.note: ずら is Nagano dialect for だろう. Standard: どこから{出|だ}すんだろう。

dialogue_setting: The {田中|たなか} house kitchen, Thursday evening: a simplified news article on {恵子|けいこ}さん's tablet.
text_title: {食料品|しょくりょうひん|groceries, food products|3}の{消費税|しょうひぜい|consumption tax|4}、1%に？

dialogue.speaker: Headline
dialogue.jp: {食料品|しょくりょうひん|groceries, food products|3}の{消費税|しょうひぜい|consumption tax|4}を8%から1%に{下げる|さげる|to lower|4}{法案|ほうあん|bill (draft law)|2}が、11{月|がつ}6{日|か}に{衆議院|しゅうぎいん|House of Representatives|2}を{通りました|とおりました}。
dialogue.en: On 6 November, a bill lowering the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% passed the House of Representatives.

dialogue.speaker: When
dialogue.jp: {下がる|さがる}のは2027{年|ねん}4{月|がつ}から2{年間|ねんかん}だけです。お{酒|さけ}と{外食|がいしょく|eating out|3}は10%のままです。
dialogue.en: It goes down only for two years, from April 2027. Alcohol and eating out stay at 10%.

dialogue.speaker: Why
dialogue.jp: {物価|ぶっか|prices (in general)|3}が{高い|たかい}{中|なか}、{家計|かけい|household budget|3}の{負担|ふたん|burden|3}を{軽く|かるく}するための{減税|げんぜい|tax cut|3}です。
dialogue.en: It's a tax cut to lighten the burden on household budgets while prices are high.

dialogue.speaker: Why 1%?
dialogue.jp: 0%ではなく1%なのは、0%だとレジの{変更|へんこう|change, alteration|3}に{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎるからだそうです。
dialogue.en: Apparently it's 1% rather than 0% because changing the cash registers for 0% would take too long.

dialogue.speaker: The other 1%
dialogue.jp: {残り|のこり|the rest, remainder|4}の1%は、{収入|しゅうにゅう|income|3}が{多くない|おおくない}{働く|はたらく}{人|ひと}にお{金|かね}を{配って|くばって|to hand out|3}{返す|かえす}{仕組み|しくみ|system, how it works|3}です。
dialogue.en: The remaining 1% will be given back by handing out money to working people on lower incomes.

dialogue.speaker: Against
dialogue.jp: {野党|やとう|opposition parties|2}はすべて{反対|はんたい}しました。お{金|かね}をどこから{出す|だす}のか、はっきりしないからです。
dialogue.en: All the opposition parties voted against it, because it isn't clear where the money will come from.

dialogue.speaker: Next
dialogue.jp: 11{日|にち}から{参議院|さんぎいん|House of Councillors|2}で{話し合い|はなしあい|discussion|3}が{始まりました|はじまりました}が、{与党|よとう|ruling parties|2}は{数|かず}が{足りない|たりない|to be not enough|4}ため、まだ{分かりません|わかりません}。
dialogue.en: Debate in the House of Councillors began on the 11th, but the ruling parties don't have enough seats, so nothing is certain yet.

listening.intro: Earlier, on the mountain, a voicemail from {恵子|けいこ}さん came in when you got signal.

lines.jp: アルちゃん、{恵子|けいこ}です。{山|やま}はどう？{紅葉|こうよう|autumn leaves|3}、きれいでしょう。
lines.en: アルちゃん, it's {恵子|けいこ}. How's the mountain? The leaves must be beautiful.

lines.jp: {明るい|あかるい}うちに{帰って|かえって}きてね。{今夜|こんや}はきのこのお{鍋|なべ|hot pot|4}よ。
lines.en: Come home while it's still light, OK? Tonight it's mushroom hot pot.

listening.question: {恵子|けいこ}さんはアルちゃんに{何|なに}をしてほしいですか。
options: {暗|くら}くなる{前|まえ}に{帰|かえ}ってくる
きのこを{買|か}ってくる
{紅葉|こうよう}の{写真|しゃしん}を{送|おく}る
listening.explain: {明|あか}るいうちに = while it's still light, so: be home before dark. The mushrooms are for dinner; nobody asks him to buy them.

grammar.form: い-adj: + うちに ({若|わか}いうちに, {温|あたた}かいうちに) · な-adj: + なうちに ({元気|げんき}なうちに) · noun: + のうちに ({学生|がくせい}のうちに) · verb: ている + うちに ({話|はな}しているうちに)
grammar.explanation: Do something while a state lasts, before it changes: {温|あたた}かいうちに = before it gets cold. Unlike {間|あいだ}に, it hints the chance won't last. With ている it also means 'while doing, without noticing': {読|よ}んでいるうちに{寝|ね}ちゃった.

examples.jp: {学生|がくせい}のうちに、いろいろな{国|くに}へ{行って|いって}みたい。
examples.en: I want to visit lots of countries while I'm still a student.

examples.jp: おばあちゃんが{元気|げんき}なうちに、{昔|むかし}の{話|はなし}をもっと{聞いて|きいて}おこう。
examples.en: While Grandma is still well, let's hear more of her old stories.

examples.jp: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞いて|きいて}いるうちに、{寝て|ねて}しまった。
examples.en: I fell asleep while listening to music.

quiz.question: スープ、{熱い|あつい}＿＿{飲んで|のんで}ね。
quiz.en: Drink the soup while it's hot.
quiz.explain: Hot now, but it won't last: うちに. までに is a deadline, ために a purpose.

quiz_more.question: {学生|がくせい}＿＿、たくさん{旅行|りょこう}したい。
quiz_more.en: I want to travel a lot while I'm a student.
quiz_more.explain: After a noun, うちに needs の: {学生|がくせい}のうちに.

quiz_more.question: {本|ほん}を{読んで|よんで}いる＿＿、{眠く|ねむく}なってきた。
quiz_more.en: While I was reading, I started getting sleepy.
quiz_more.explain: ているうちに: while doing something, a change creeps in without you noticing.

kanji.where: On every supermarket and konbini receipt: food items marked ※ or ＊ with the note {軽減税率|けいげんぜいりつ}{対象|たいしょう}, 'reduced rate applies'.
kanji.related: {消費税|しょうひぜい} = consumption tax; {税込|ぜいこみ} = tax included; {税抜|ぜいぬ}き = before tax.
kanji.breakdown: {軽減税率|けいげんぜいりつ}: 軽 light + 減 reduce (軽減 = lighten) + 税 tax + 率 rate → 'lightened tax rate'.

tip.title: Eating in? That's 10%
tip.body: Since 2019 food is taxed at 8%, but eating it in the shop counts as 外食 at 10%. That's why konbini and fast-food staff ask {店内|てんない}でお{召|め}し{上|あ}がりですか? ('Eating in?'). Say {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りで for take-away.

challenge.prompt: {田中|たなか}さん looks at the tablet and grumbles: 「なんで0%にしないんだ？」 Pass on the reason from the article.
challenge.model_answer: レジの{変更|へんこう|change, alteration|3}に{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎるからだそうです。

options.jp: レジの{変更|へんこう}に{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎるからだそうです。
options.why: Reason + から, then だそうです: 'apparently it's because…'. Polite, and makes clear it's from the article.

options.jp: レジの{変更|へんこう}に{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎるだからだそうです。
options.why: No だ between a verb and から: かかりすぎるから.

options.jp: レジの{変更|へんこう}に{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎるうちにだそうです。
レジの{変更|へんこう}に{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎるためでございます。
options.why: でございます is hotel-staff keigo: far too stiff at the family dinner table.

challenge.explanation: {時間|じかん}がかかりすぎる = it takes too long; から gives the reason, and だそうです marks it as something you read, not your own idea. です keeps it polite with your host without sounding stiff.

vocab.note: {消費|しょうひ} consume + {税|ぜい} tax. Prices say {税込|ぜいこみ} (tax in) or {税抜|ぜいぬ}き (tax out).
Someone lowers something (を{下|さ}げる); by itself it goes down: {下|さ}がる.
{外|そと} outside + {食|た}べる. {外食|がいしょく}する = to eat out.
Money, work or worry. {負担|ふたん}が{大|おお}きい / {軽|かる}くする. {体|からだ}に{負担|ふたん} = hard on the body.
Formal 'change' for plans and settings: {予定|よてい}の{変更|へんこう}. In speech often {変|か}える.
From {残|のこ}る (to remain). {残|のこ}りもの = leftovers.
Flyers, food, money to many people. {気|き}を{配|くば}る = to be attentive.
How a machine or system works: どういう{仕組|しく}み？ = how does that work?
Mostly heard as {足|た}りない: お{金|かね}が{足|た}りない, {寝|ね}{足|た}りない.

vocab.en: to be a help, a relief
vocab.note: Thanking for help in daily life: {助|たす}かります！ = that really helps!

kanji_study.parts: 酉 sake jar (also the 'bird' of the zodiac) + 己 a kneeling person → someone kneeling by the sake jar, pouring it out for everyone: distribute, hand out.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 酒 (sake): 配 has 己 on the right, 酒 has the water radical 氵 on the left.

kanji_study.parts: 尸 a roof / doorway (the 'corpse' radical, here just a building) + 由 'from, reason' → something coming from outside reaches your door: reach, deliver.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 屈 (bend): 届 has 由 under the roof, 屈 has 出.

extras.title: Words from the news
extras.intro: Politics words you'll hear in every evening news programme.

items.jp: {与党|よとう|ruling party|2}と{野党|やとう|opposition party|2}
items.note: {与|よ} take part + {党|とう} party; {野|や} field → 'outside the government'.

items.jp: {法案|ほうあん|bill (draft law)|2}が{成立する|せいりつする|to be passed into law|2}
items.en: a bill is passed into law

items.note: Two houses: {衆議院|しゅうぎいん} and {参議院|さんぎいん}.

items.jp: {税込|ぜいこみ|tax included|3}・{税抜|ぜいぬき|before tax|3}
items.note: Check which one a price tag shows!

extras.title: Giving reasons
extras.title_jp: {理由|りゆう}の{言い方|いいかた}

items.jp: {高い|たかい}から、{買わない|かわない}。
items.en: It's expensive, so I won't buy it.
items.note: から: everyday, your own reason.

items.jp: {雨|あめ}なので、{中止|ちゅうし|cancellation|3}です。
items.note: ので: softer, polite, good for excuses.

items.jp: {数|かず}が{足りない|たりない|to be not enough|4}ため、まだ{分かりません|わかりません}。
items.en: Because the numbers aren't enough, it's still unclear.
items.note: ため: written and news style.

items.jp: 1%なのは、{時間|じかん}がかかるからだ。
items.en: The reason it's 1% is that it takes time.
